summary: Comprehensive testing of Trusted Devices / Active Sessions feature completed. All 13 session management backend tests passed (100%). All 19 MFA/password reset regression tests passed (100%). Frontend UI tests verified the Security Settings page displays the Trusted devices & active sessions panel correctly with session metadata, revoke controls, and proper current session marking.
critical_code_review_comments: Session tracking correctly creates auth_sessions on register and login with session ID embedded in JWT
GET /api/auth/sessions returns proper metadata: device_name, browser, os, ip_address, mfa_verified, timestamps, is_current flag, risk_flags
POST /api/auth/logout correctly revokes current session and invalidates token
POST /api/auth/sessions/revoke-all correctly revokes all other sessions while preserving current session
Token validation in get_current_company() properly checks session revocation status
Security Settings page displays Trusted devices & active sessions panel with all required UI elements
Current session is marked with 'Current' badge and has no revoke button (correct UX)
MFA verified vs Password only badges display correctly based on session.mfa_verified
Risk flags (new-location, password-only) are displayed when applicable

test_credentials.note: Multiple test accounts created during testing with prefix session_test_, ui_session_test_, ui_revoke_test_, ui_logout_test_, ui_multi_session_

seed_data_creation: Multiple test accounts created during testing for session management verification
context_for_next_testing_agent: Session management feature is fully functional. All session tracking, revocation, and token invalidation flows work correctly. MFA and password reset features remain functional after session tracking changes. The Security Settings page correctly displays the Trusted devices & active sessions panel with all required metadata and controls.

session_creation.on_register: Creates auth_session with session_id in JWT
session_creation.on_login: Creates new auth_session with session_id in JWT

get_sessions_api.returns: current_session_id and items array with session metadata

logout_api.behavior: Revokes current session, token becomes invalid for /auth/me

revoke_session_api.behavior: Revokes specific session, that session's token becomes invalid

revoke_all_api.behavior: Revokes all sessions except current, current session remains valid

token_invalidation.after_revoke_all: Other sessions' tokens fail, current session token still works
